bill.title: To amend the Richard B. Russell National School Lunch Act to require schools participating in the school lunch program or school breakfast program to publish information on any menu item or food offered or served in a lunch or breakfast, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

classification.plainSummary: This bill would require schools that participate in the federal school lunch or breakfast programs to publish information about every menu item or food they offer or serve. The bill does not specify what information must be published (such as nutritional content, ingredients, or sourcing) or how it must be made available to families and students.

industries.rationale: Schools participating in federal meal programs would face new disclosure obligations for all menu items served.
Food suppliers to school meal programs may need to provide additional product information to help schools meet disclosure requirements.
Food service companies and vendors supplying school cafeterias would be affected by new information-reporting requirements.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
